topics.title: Introduction, Scope and Exclusions of AS 9
explain: AS 9 is a mandatory standard governing the timing and measurement of revenue recognition in Profit & Loss.
Revenue arises from ordinary business activities: sale of goods, rendering of services, and resource use by others.
AS 9 excludes construction contracts, hire-purchase and lease agreements, government grants, and insurance contracts.
It also excludes revaluation gains, asset sales, foreign exchange gains, and natural increases in agricultural products.

flow.title: Checking Scope Applicability of AS 9
steps: Identify ordinary revenue transaction
Check if covered by specific standard
Exclude construction leases insurance grants
Exclude asset revaluations and forex gains
Apply AS 9 if standard criteria met

topics.example: Entity XY sells a factory machine for ₹2 lakh (book value ₹1.80 lakh). The ₹20,000 gain is a capital receipt/gain on disposal, not AS 9 ordinary revenue.
remember: AS 9 is mandatory for all enterprises.
Construction contracts, leases, insurance, and grants are excluded from AS 9.
mistakes: Treating gain on sale of fixed assets as ordinary revenue instead of Other Income/Gain.

quiz.q: Which of the following is covered under AS 9?
quiz.why: AS 9 explicitly covers rendering of services, while construction, leases, and grants are excluded.

quiz.q: A company recognized gain on revaluation of fixed assets as revenue. Is this correct under AS 9?
o: No, holding gains are excluded from AS 9 revenue.
quiz.why: AS 9 specifically excludes realized and unrealized holding gains on non-current assets from the definition of revenue.

topics.title: Definition of Revenue and Agency Relationships
explain: Revenue is the gross inflow of cash, receivables, or other consideration from ordinary business activities.
In an agency relationship, revenue is the commission earned, not the gross cash collected from customers.
A principal bears inventory and quality risks and is obligated to supply the goods or services.
An agent merely arranges the transaction and does not take on primary performance risk.

flow.title: Determining Principal vs Agent Revenue Status
steps: Evaluate transaction responsibility
Check who bears inventory and quality risks
If primary obligor recognize gross revenue
If facilitating party recognize commission only

topics.example: Zigato collects ₹300 lakhs (₹200 food, ₹60 delivery, ₹40 GST). Zigato recognizes ₹60 lakhs delivery revenue as agent, while the restaurant recognizes ₹200 lakhs.
remember: GST and collected taxes are third-party liabilities, not revenue.
Agents recognize only their commission or delivery fee as revenue.
mistakes: Recognizing gross collections as revenue when acting merely as an agent.

quiz.q: What is the revenue for an agent in a transaction?
o: Cost of goods sold plus markup
quiz.why: In an agency relationship, revenue is limited to the commission earned, not the gross inflow.

quiz.q: Trip Deal buys 100 airline tickets at its own risk of unsold tickets and resells them. How should it recognize revenue?
o: Recognize total sales price of tickets as revenue
Postpone revenue until all tickets sell
quiz.why: Since Trip Deal bears the risks and rewards of unsold tickets, it acts as a principal and recognizes total sales revenue.

topics.title: Revenue Recognition for Sale of Goods
explain: Sale of goods revenue is recognized when performance criteria are satisfied and collection is reasonably certain.
Performance requires transferring property/ownership or significant risks and rewards to the buyer.
The seller must retain no effective control usually associated with ownership.
If ultimate collection is uncertain at performance time, revenue recognition must be postponed.

flow.title: Sale of Goods Recognition Process
steps: Transfer risks and rewards to buyer
Relinquish effective control of goods
Determine consideration amount with certainty
Assess collectability at sale date
Recognize revenue if all conditions met

topics.example: AB sold goods to CD on 1st Jan for ₹2 lakh when collection was clear. If CD goes into liquidation on 15th March, AB keeps the revenue and records a bad debt expense.
remember: Postpone revenue if collection is uncertain at performance date.
If uncertainty arises after sale date, record bad debts expense instead of reversing revenue.
mistakes: Reversing previously recognized valid revenue when a bad debt occurs later.

quiz.q: When should revenue from sale of goods be postponed?
o: When goods are delivered to buyer
When seller gives a trade discount
When ultimate collection is unreasonably uncertain at performance
When payment is received in advance
quiz.why: Revenue recognition must be postponed if ultimate collection is not reasonably certain at the time of performance.

quiz.q: AB sold goods to CD on 1st March when CD had major financial issues and collection was uncertain. CD secured bank funding on 5th May. When is revenue recognized?
quiz.why: Revenue is postponed on 1st March due to collection uncertainty and recognized on 5th May when uncertainty is removed.

topics.title: Revenue Recognition for Rendering of Services
explain: Service revenue is recognized as service is performed using one of two accounting methods.
Proportionate Completion Method recognizes revenue proportionately with the performance of each act.
Completed Service Contract Method recognizes revenue only when the contract is completed or substantially completed.
Completed service method applies when performance consists of executing a single act or critical final act.

flow.title: Choosing Service Revenue Method
steps: Identify number of acts in service
If single act wait for completion
If multiple acts measure degree of completion
Recognize revenue proportionately or on completion
Postpone revenue if collection is uncertain

topics.example: A firm installing a complex machine uses the completed service contract method and recognizes revenue only after final testing and installation.
remember: Proportionate completion applies when service consists of execution of more than one act.
Completed service contract method applies when performance consists of a single act.
mistakes: Recognizing revenue on a single-act service before the final performance act is complete.

quiz.q: Which method recognizes service revenue proportionately as each act is performed?
quiz.why: Proportionate Completion Method recognizes revenue proportionately based on the degree of completion of multiple acts.

quiz.q: An entity agrees to repair a complex machine (single-act performance). Which revenue method should be used?
quiz.why: For single-act service execution, the Completed Service Contract Method must be used.

topics.title: Revenue from Interest, Royalties, and Dividends
explain: Revenue from enterprise resources used by others is recognized when no significant collectability uncertainty exists.
Interest revenue is recognized on a time proportion basis considering principal outstanding and applicable rate.
Royalty revenue is recognized on an accrual basis according to the terms of the relevant agreement.
Dividend revenue is recognized when the owner's legal right to receive payment is established (declaration date).

flow.title: Resource Revenue Recognition Test
steps: Identify type of resource revenue
For Interest calculate on time proportion
For Royalties accrue per agreement terms
For Dividends check formal declaration date
Recognize revenue when collectability is clear

topics.example: Mutual fund dividend proposed on 10th April and declared on 15th June 20X1 is recognized on 15th June 20X1 when the right to receive payment is established.
remember: Interest is calculated on time proportion.
Dividends are recognized when the right to receive is established, not on proposal.
mistakes: Recognizing proposed dividends before formal declaration.

quiz.q: On what basis should interest income be recognized under AS 9?
quiz.why: AS 9 requires interest to be recognized on a time proportion basis taking into account amount outstanding and rate applicable.

quiz.q: When is dividend revenue recognized in the books of an investor?
o: When dividend is proposed by directors
When right to receive payment is established
At the end of financial year
When cash is deposited into bank
quiz.why: Dividend revenue is recognized only when the owner's right to receive payment is established.

topics.title: Special Conditions for Sale of Goods
explain: Delayed Delivery: Recognize revenue at sale date if buyer takes title, goods are identified, ready, and delayed at buyer's request.
Sale on Approval: Recognize revenue only upon formal acceptance or expiry of approval time limit.
Inspection/Installation: Recognize upon completion if installation is complex; recognize at sale if simple.
Sale & Repurchase: Treat as a financing loan arrangement; recognize borrowing, not sales revenue.
Discounts & Consignment: Deduct trade discounts from turnover; record cash discounts as expense. Recognize consignment revenue only when agent sells to third party.

flow.title: Evaluating Specific Sales Transactions
steps: Check transaction category and terms
Assess risk transfer and conditions
If sale-repurchase treat as loan
If consignment wait for ultimate sale
Apply specific AS 9 rule for recognition

topics.example: KJ sells goods for ₹5 lakhs agreeing to repurchase at ₹6 lakhs in 3 months. KJ records Bank Dr. ₹5L to Loan Cr. ₹5L and ₹1L interest expense.
remember: Sale and repurchase arrangements are financing transactions.
Trade discounts are deducted from sales; cash discounts are recorded as expense.
mistakes: Deducting cash discounts directly from total sales turnover.

quiz.q: How should a sale and repurchase agreement be accounted for by the seller under AS 9?
o: Recognize sale revenue and cost of goods sold
quiz.why: Sale and repurchase agreements are financing arrangements, so borrowing is recognized instead of sale.

quiz.q: Goods sent on consignment worth ₹10,00,000; consignee sold goods worth ₹5,50,000. How much revenue can the consignor recognize?
quiz.why: Consignment revenue is recognized only for goods actually sold to third parties (₹5,50,000).

topics.title: Revenue Uncertainties and Disclosure Requirements
explain: If ultimate collection cannot be assessed with reasonable certainty when raising a claim, postpone revenue recognition.
When consideration is not determinable within reasonable limits, postpone revenue recognition.
When uncertainty resolves later, recognize revenue in the current period (not as a prior period item).
Disclose circumstances where revenue recognition has been postponed pending resolution of uncertainties (alongside AS 1).

flow.title: Managing Uncertainties and Disclosures
steps: Assess collectability at claim date
If uncertain postpone revenue recognition
Disclose reason for postponement in notes
Monitor until uncertainty resolves
Recognize revenue in period certainty achieved

topics.example: Railway claim of ₹2,00,000 lodged in 20X1 passed for ₹1,50,000 in 20X3. Recognize ₹1,50,000 as revenue in 20X3 (not prior period) and disclose separately.
remember: Postponed revenue is recognized in the period it becomes reasonably certain.
Disclose postponed revenue circumstances in financial statement notes.
mistakes: Treating eventual collection of a postponed uncertain claim as a prior period adjustment.

quiz.q: When revenue recognition is postponed due to uncertainty, when is it recognized?
o: In the period when collection becomes reasonably certain
As a prior period adjustment in past year
quiz.why: Postponed revenue is recognized as revenue of the period in which collection becomes reasonably certain.

quiz.q: What disclosure is required under AS 9 regarding postponed revenue?
o: Disclose circumstances in which revenue recognition has been postponed
quiz.why: AS 9 mandates disclosing the circumstances in which revenue recognition has been postponed pending resolution of uncertainties.
